questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'service' in the context of IT Service Management?

options.text: A software application installed on user devices
A capability provided by IT to meet a business need
A hardware component in the data center
A support ticket submitted by an end user

explanation.correct: A service is defined as a capability provided by an IT organization to meet a particular business need. Examples include email, network access, software applications, and cloud storage. This aligns with ITIL best practices for service-oriented IT delivery.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A software application may be part of delivering a service, but a service is a broader capability meeting business needs
Hardware components are assets or CIs that support services, but are not services themselves
A support ticket is a request or incident, which is a different ITSM concept from a service

source.excerpt: A service is a capability provided by an IT organization to meet a particular business need. A few examples of this are email, network access, software applications, and cloud storage.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the CMDB and CSDM in ServiceNow?

options.text: CSDM replaces the CMDB in newer ServiceNow releases
CSDM is a framework that enhances how data is modeled in the CMDB
CMDB is a subset of CSDM that stores only hardware assets
CSDM and CMDB are separate products that cannot be used together

explanation.correct: CSDM (Common Service Data Model) is a best-practice framework for CMDB data modeling and management. It enhances the CMDB by providing standardized terms, definitions, and relationships that link business and technical aspects. CSDM is not code to install but guidelines for modeling data within the CMDB.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CSDM does not replace the CMDB. It is a framework that works with and enhances the CMDB
The CMDB stores all configuration items including software, services, and relationships, not just hardware
CSDM is specifically designed to work with the CMDB, not as a separate product

source.excerpt: CSDM is essentially a framework that enhances your CMDB, making it easier to manage and utilize over time... CSDM is neither a code to be installed nor a standalone product. It also doesn't serve as an implementation guide for current ServiceNow applications. Instead, it's a set of guidelines specifically created to assist in modeling data within the CMDB.

questions.question: Which applications are included in ITSM Standard but NOT in ITSM Pro or Enterprise exclusively? (Select two)

explanation.correct: ITSM Standard includes core applications: Incident Management, Problem Management, Change Management, Asset and Cost Management, and Request Management. ITSM Pro adds advanced capabilities like Predictive Intelligence (AI-powered routing) and Virtual Agent with AI capabilities. ITSM Pro includes all Standard features plus the advanced ones.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Predictive Intelligence is a Pro/Enterprise feature that uses machine learning for automatic ticket routing
Virtual Agent with AI-powered natural language processing is a Pro/Enterprise feature. Standard only includes basic keyword-based chatbot

source.excerpt: The primary applications included in ITSM standard are displayed on the left, comprising incident problem, change management, asset and cost management, and request management. ITSM Pro offers a range of additional capabilities, including our advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning features.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Service Portfolio Management in ServiceNow ITSM?

options.text: To consolidate information for managing and organizing services
To generate performance reports for management

explanation.correct: Service Portfolio Management is a centralized application that consolidates information for portfolio managers and service owners to develop a service pipeline aligned with organizational requirements. It helps prevent service duplication and overlap, enables identification and retirement of low-value services, and allows resources to be repurposed efficiently.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incident escalation is managed within Incident Management, not Service Portfolio Management
Change approval workflows are configured in Change Management
Performance reports are generated through Reporting and Performance Analytics, not Service Portfolio Management

source.excerpt: Service Portfolio Management is a centralized application that consolidates the necessary information for portfolio managers and service owners to develop a service pipeline that aligns with the organization's most significant requirements. This system helps prevent service duplication and overlap, enabling the prompt identification and retirement of low-value services.

questions.question: Which persona is responsible for ensuring that processes are followed and run efficiently in ServiceNow ITSM?

explanation.correct: The Process Manager is responsible for ensuring that processes are followed and run efficiently. They may be the assigned manager of one or more groups. Process Owners, by contrast, are responsible for creating process models and identifying KPIs. Service Owners are responsible for the entirety of a service.

wrongAnswers.explanation: End Users are internal or external users who access the service desk through the portal. They report issues but don't manage processes
Agent Fulfillers belong to specialized groups like software or hardware teams. They resolve tasks but don't manage processes
Service Owners are responsible for entire services and ensuring data integrity, not process efficiency

source.excerpt: Moving on, let's talk about process owners. These individuals hold the responsibility for one or more processes... the process manager, who is responsible for ensuring that processes are followed and run efficiently. They may be the assigned manager of one or more groups.

questions.question: What is the ITIL role in ServiceNow used for?

options.text: To provide administrative access to all platform features
To enable help desk agents to perform standard ITSM interactions
To grant read-only access to incident records
To allow users to approve change requests

explanation.correct: The ITIL role is the fundamental ITSM role that allows individuals to perform standard interactions for a help desk agent. Users with this role can open, update, and close incidents, problems, changes, and configuration management items. Out of the box, only users with the ITIL role can have tasks assigned to them.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The admin role provides access to all features and capabilities, not the ITIL role
Read-only access would be a different role. ITIL provides read-write access to ITSM records
Change approval requires specific approval group membership, not just the ITIL role

source.excerpt: When considering the base roles, we refer to ITIL as the fundamental ITSM role... Users with the ITIL role can perform standard interactions for an help desk agent. This out-of-the-box technician role allows individuals to open, update, and close incidents, problems, changes, configuration management items, et cetera.

questions.question: Which are the five domains of CSDM (Common Service Data Model)? (Select two correct domains)

explanation.correct: CSDM contains five interconnected domains: 1) Foundations - underlying data layer, 2) Design - planning and investing in digital products, 3) Build - development details, 4) Sell/Consume - services available in the catalog, and 5) Manage Technical Services - deployed instances and infrastructure. Incident and Remediation are not CSDM domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incident is an ITSM process/application, not a CSDM domain. CSDM focuses on service modeling, not incident handling
Remediation is not a CSDM domain. The five domains are Foundations, Design, Build, Sell/Consume, and Manage Technical Services

source.excerpt: CSDM contains five interconnected domains. CSDM domains represent how data is grouped within the data model. First is the Foundations domain... The Design domain is responsible for planning and investing in digital products... After Design is the Build domain... In the Sell/Consume domain... Moving on to the Manage Technical Services domain.

questions.question: An organization wants to provide employees with a unified interface for submitting IT requests, HR requests, and Facilities requests. Which ServiceNow interface is designed for this purpose?

explanation.correct: The Employee Center Portal is a versatile and interactive portal designed for service delivery and employee engagement across multiple departments. It enables organizations to organize service solutions across departments like IT, HR, Workplace, Legal, and Procurement with digital workflows.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Operations Workspace is designed for agents to manage IT service workflows, not for employees to submit requests
Now Mobile Agent is for service agents to complete tasks from anywhere, not for employees to submit cross-departmental requests
CMDB is a repository for configuration items, not an interface for submitting requests

source.excerpt: The ServiceNow Employee Center Portal, a versatile and interactive portal designed for service delivery and employee engagement across multiple departments. The Employee Center Portal also enables customers to quickly organize their service solutions across departments, such as IT, HR, Workplace, Legal, and Procurement, with digital workflows.

questions.question: Which two schedule types are commonly used for On-Call Scheduling in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: ServiceNow On-Call Scheduling supports 24/7 schedules for organizations seeking continuous task coverage and follow-the-sun schedules that cater to various time zones for global support. Holidays can also be managed to allow shift users to take time off.

wrongAnswers.explanation: While business-hours scheduling exists in ServiceNow, the course specifically highlights 24/7 and follow-the-sun as the two primary on-call schedule types.
Seasonal rotation is not specifically mentioned as a standard on-call scheduling type.

source.excerpt: An organization seeking continuous task coverage could opt for a 24/7 schedule, while those providing global support may prefer a follow the sun schedule.

questions.question: Which application allows service owners to track and analyze how services are performing from a single integrated interface?

explanation.correct: Service Owner Workspace provides service owners with a single window to manage and monitor portfolios and services in one integrated and graphically intuitive user interface. It allows tracking and analyzing service performance and identifying services that need attention.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Performance Analytics provides data visualizations to anticipate trends, but Service Owner Workspace is the dedicated service management interface.
Vendor Manager Workspace is for tracking vendor performance, not overall service performance.
Service Portfolio Management manages the service catalog and offerings, but doesn't provide the same operational monitoring interface.

source.excerpt: Service owner workspace provides service owners with a single window to manage and monitor portfolios and services in one integrated and graphically intuitive user interface.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Now Mobile application for ITSM?

options.text: View request status and requested items

explanation.correct: Now Mobile allows users to view request status, submit/track requests, complete tasks/surveys/assessments, and receive notifications. Managing incident escalation workflows is an administrative function done in the desktop interface, not the end-user mobile app.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Now Mobile home tab displays request status, requested items, and approvals.
The services tab allows users to submit and track requests and browse available services.
Users can complete assigned tasks, surveys, and assessments through Now Mobile.

source.excerpt: The application features a home tab that displays request status, requested items, and approvals, and a services tab that allows users to submit and track requests.

questions.question: What capability does the Now Agent mobile app provide that distinguishes it from the Now Mobile app?

options.text: It allows end users to submit service requests
It enables IT agents to work on incidents from mobile/tablet devices with offline capability
It provides access to the Service Catalog
It sends push notifications for approvals

explanation.correct: Now Agent is designed for IT service agents (resolvers), enabling them to access incidents via mobile and tablet devices, work offline, and track their location. Now Mobile is for end users; Now Agent is for resolvers.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Submitting service requests is a Now Mobile feature for end users, not Now Agent.
Service Catalog access is available in Now Mobile and the desktop interface, not specific to Now Agent.
Push notifications are available in both Now Mobile and Now Agent, not a distinguishing feature.

source.excerpt: The Now Agent app liberates it service agents from being tied to their desks, enabling them to work while on the move... allows users to work offline and track their location.

questions.question: What are the four key elements that a well-executed ITSM program covers?
questions.explanation: According to ServiceNow ITSM fundamentals, a well-executed ITSM program covers four key elements: People, Processes, Products, and Partners. These represent the foundational pillars needed for effective IT service delivery.

wrongAnswers.Planning, Design, Creation, and Operatio: These represent the stages of ITSM implementation, not the four key elements of an ITSM program.
wrongAnswers.Cost, Innovation, Resilience, and Experi: These are the four primary drivers/challenges facing IT organizations, not the elements of an ITSM program.
wrongAnswers.Incidents, Problems, Changes, and Reques: These are ITSM process types/applications, not the four key elements of an ITSM program.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Incident Management and Problem Management in ServiceNow?
options: Incident Management focuses on restoring services quickly; Problem Management focuses on finding the root cause to prevent future incidents
Incident Management handles hardware issues; Problem Management handles software issues
Incident Management is reactive only; Problem Management is proactive only
Incident Management is for end users; Problem Management is for IT staff
questions.correctAnswer: Incident Management focuses on restoring services quickly; Problem Management focuses on finding the root cause to prevent future incidents
questions.explanation: Incident Management focuses on restoring services as quickly as possible rather than preventing or mitigating the incident. Problem Management focuses on finding ways to prevent incidents from happening by identifying the root or underlying cause of one or more incidents.

wrongAnswers.Incident Management handles hardware iss: Both processes handle all types of issues regardless of whether they involve hardware or software.
wrongAnswers.Incident Management is reactive only; Pr: While Incident Management is primarily reactive, Problem Management can be both proactive (preventing incidents) and reactive (investigating causes of occurred incidents).
wrongAnswers.Incident Management is for end users; Pr: Both processes involve multiple personas including end users, agents, and managers. End users report incidents, and problem records can be created from incident trend analysis.

questions.question: Which TWO applications are exclusively available in ITSM Enterprise and NOT included in ITSM Pro? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: ITSM Enterprise adds two exclusive capabilities on top of Pro and Standard: Process Mining (visual analysis of process flows to identify bottlenecks) and Workforce Optimization (scheduling teams efficiently while tracking performance capacity). Continual Improvement and Vendor Management are ITSM Pro features.

wrongAnswers.Continual Improvement: Continual Improvement is included in ITSM Pro, not exclusively in ITSM Enterprise.
wrongAnswers.Vendor Management: Vendor Management is included in ITSM Pro, not exclusively in ITSM Enterprise.

questions.question: A Cloud Dimensions consultant is configuring The Country Store's ServiceNow instance. They need to allow agents to handle incidents, problems, changes, requests, and walk-ups from a single interface. Which workspace should they configure?
questions.explanation: Service Operations Workspace (SOW) is a versatile workspace that manages various task records like incidents, problems, changes, requests, and walk-ups throughout the lifecycle of these workflows. Note that Agent Workspace is no longer available and has been replaced by Service Operations Workspace.

wrongAnswers.IT Service Management Workspace: There is no specific workspace by this name. Service Operations Workspace is the designated workspace for handling multiple ITSM workflows.
wrongAnswers.Agent Workspace: Agent Workspace is no longer available. It has been replaced by Service Operations Workspace as the new workspace solution for agents.
wrongAnswers.Employee Center: Employee Center is a self-service portal for employees to make requests and access information, not a workspace for agents to manage ITSM tasks.

questions.question: What are the three main benefits of implementing ITSM according to ServiceNow?
options: Cost reduction, enhanced productivity, and improved IT support
Faster deployments, fewer incidents, and better security
More automation, less downtime, and higher compliance
Better reporting, improved SLAs, and reduced headcount
questions.correctAnswer: Cost reduction, enhanced productivity, and improved IT support
questions.explanation: According to ServiceNow ITSM fundamentals, the three main benefits of ITSM are: (1) Cost reduction — utilizing ITSM applications to improve experiences while staying within financial constraints, (2) Enhanced productivity — integrating AI and virtual agent capabilities, and (3) Enhancement of IT support.

wrongAnswers.Faster deployments, fewer incidents, and: While these may be indirect outcomes, the three stated benefits of ITSM are cost reduction, enhanced productivity, and improved IT support.
wrongAnswers.More automation, less downtime, and high: These are not the three main benefits identified by ServiceNow for ITSM implementation.
wrongAnswers.Better reporting, improved SLAs, and red: These are not the three main benefits. ITSM focuses on cost reduction, productivity, and IT support improvement, not headcount reduction.

questions.question: Which THREE types of changes are defined in ServiceNow Change Management? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow defines three types of changes: Normal changes (follow a prescriptive process with reviews, assessments, and approvals), Standard changes (pre-authorized, low-risk, common changes following specific procedures), and Emergency changes (necessary to resolve major incidents or implement security patches, requiring immediate implementation).

wrongAnswers.Expedited: Expedited is not a defined change type in ServiceNow. Emergency changes cover urgent scenarios.
wrongAnswers.Scheduled: Scheduled is not a change type. Maintenance schedules and blackout windows are separate concepts that specify when changes should or should not occur.
